people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch named in the covenant formula of the opening letter.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Patriarch named in the covenant formula of the opening letter.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Patriarch named in the covenant formula of the opening letter.

people.name: Demetrius
people.description: Seleucid king in whose reign (year 169) an earlier letter to the Jews of Egypt was written.
people.identity_note: 1:7 is dated to Seleucid year 169 (c. 143 BCE), which falls in the reign of Demetrius II, not Demetrius I of ch. 14. Kept separate from demetrius-i-soter.

people.name: Jason
people.description: Brother of Onias who bought the high priesthood from Antiochus IV, hellenized Jerusalem, was outbid by Menelaus and died in exile.
people.identity_note: 1:7 'Jason and his company revolted from the holy land' is traditionally taken as this Jason; included here. Brother of Onias (4:7, 4:26) but no parent is named in 2MA. Same new_id used in 4MA.

people.name: Judas
people.description: Jewish resistance leader who purified the temple and defeated Nicanor, Timotheus, Gorgias and others.
people.identity_note: The 'Judas' of the letter in 1:10 (and 2:14) is usually taken as Judas Maccabeus, though the letter's date has led some to propose another Judas; merged here. His brothers Simon, Joseph and Jonathan are named in 8:22; his father is not named in 2MA. Reviewer: reconcile id with the 1MA census.

people.name: Aristobulus
people.description: Teacher of King Ptolemy, of priestly descent, addressee of the second prefatory letter.
people.identity_note: Traditionally identified with the Jewish philosopher Aristobulus of Alexandria.

people.name: Ptolemy
people.description: Ptolemaic king of Egypt, whose enthronement Apollonius attended and to whom Philip fled.
people.identity_note: 1:10 'King Ptolemy' (pupil of Aristobulus) is traditionally Ptolemy VI Philometor; merged with the named Philometor of 4:21, 9:29, 10:13. Same new_id used in 4MA 4:22.

people.name: Antiochus
people.description: Seleucid king who persecuted the Jews, profaned the temple, and died in agony after retreating from Persia.
people.identity_note: The prefatory letter (1:13-16) reports an Antiochus killed in the temple of Nanaea; it is traditionally read as Antiochus IV despite conflicting with ch. 9's account of his death (some scholars suggest Antiochus III or VII). Merged here with that caveat. His father (9:23 'my father', not named) is not recorded. In 4MA 4:15 he is called son of Seleucus. Same new_id used in 4MA.

people.name: Nehemiah
people.description: Legend of Nehemiah rekindling the altar fire and founding a library.
people.identity_note: The governor Nehemiah of the book of Nehemiah; 2MA attributes temple and altar building to him.

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Priest who led the prayer at Nehemiah's sacrifice of the rekindled fire.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Jonathan brother of Judas (8:22).

people.name: Moses
people.description: Lawgiver cited as precedent and author of the law.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.description: Prophet who in legend hid the tabernacle, ark and altar of incense, and appears in Judas' dream giving him a gold sword.

people.name: Solomon
people.description: King cited for his temple-dedication prayer and eight-day feast.

people.name: David
people.description: King whose writings Nehemiah collected.

people.name: Jason of Cyrene
people.description: Author of a five-volume history that 2 Maccabees abridges.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Jason the high priest.

people.name: Antiochus Eupator
people.description: Son and successor of Antiochus IV who campaigned against Judea with Lysias and was later killed by Demetrius.
people.identity_note: Antiochus IV calls him 'my son Antiochus' (9:25); 'Eupator his son' (2:20). 'Antiochus' in 11:22, 11:27, 13:3, 13:4 and 14:2 refers to him.

people.name: Onias
people.description: Pious high priest during Heliodorus' visit, supplanted by his brother Jason and murdered by Andronicus at Daphne.
people.identity_note: Conventionally Onias III. Brother of Jason (4:7). Father not named in 2MA. Appears posthumously in Judas' dream (15:12-14). Same new_id used in 4MA.

people.name: Seleucus
people.description: Seleucid king who funded the temple sacrifices and sent Heliodorus to seize the treasury.
people.identity_note: Seleucus IV. Father of Demetrius I (14:1). Same new_id used in 4MA.

people.name: Simon
people.description: Benjamite guardian of the temple who informed against the treasury and slandered Onias; brother of Menelaus.
people.identity_note: 'Of the tribe of Benjamin' (3:4); some Latin/Armenian witnesses read 'Bilgah' (a priestly course). Brother of Menelaus (4:23). Same new_id used in 4MA 4:1-5. Distinct from Simon brother of Judas.

people.name: Apollonius of Tarsus
people.description: Governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia to whom Simon reported the temple treasury.
people.identity_note: Greek manuscripts read 'Apollonius son of Thraseas'; WEB renders 'of Tarsus'. Possibly the same as Apollonius son of Menestheus (4:4), who holds the same governorship, but the patronymics differ, so kept separate. 4MA 4:2-14 retells this episode with Apollonius himself entering the temple; mapped to this id in 4MA.

people.name: Heliodorus
people.description: Chancellor of Seleucus IV, struck down when trying to seize the temple treasury.

people.name: Hyrcanus
people.description: Wealthy man whose money was deposited in the temple treasury.

people.name: Tobias
people.description: Father of Hyrcanus.
people.identity_note: Head of the Tobiad family; not identified with Tobiah the Ammonite of Nehemiah (centuries earlier) or with Tobias of the book of Tobit.

people.name: Apollonius son of Menestheus
people.description: Governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, sent to Egypt for Philometor's enthronement.
people.identity_note: See identity_note on Apollonius of Tarsus.

people.name: Menestheus
people.description: Father of Apollonius.

people.name: John the father of Eupolemus
people.description: Father of Eupolemus, who obtained royal privileges for the Jews.

people.name: Eupolemus
people.description: Envoy to the Romans to establish friendship and alliance.

people.name: Menelaus
people.description: Brother of Simon who outbid Jason for the high priesthood, stole temple vessels and was executed at Beroea.
people.identity_note: Brother of Simon the temple guardian (4:23) and of Lysimachus (4:29).

people.name: Sostratus
people.description: Commander of the Jerusalem citadel responsible for collecting revenues.

people.name: Lysimachus
people.description: Brother and deputy of Menelaus, killed by a mob after temple sacrileges.

people.name: Crates
people.description: Commander over the Cyprians, left as deputy by Sostratus.

people.name: Antiochis
people.description: Concubine of Antiochus IV to whom Tarsus and Mallus were given.

people.name: Andronicus
people.description: High-ranking deputy of Antiochus IV who murdered Onias and was executed for it.
people.identity_note: Executed in 4:38, so distinct from Andronicus the governor at Gerizim (5:23).

people.name: Hauran
people.description: Aged man who led Lysimachus' armed force.
people.identity_note: Personal name (some translations 'Auranus'); not the region Hauran.

people.name: Ptolemy son of Dorymenes
people.description: Seleucid official bribed by Menelaus; later governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia who sent Nicanor and Gorgias.
people.identity_note: 6:8 ('by the suggestion of Ptolemy') and 8:8-9 ('Ptolemy, the governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia') are assigned here because 1 Macc 3:38 names Ptolemy son of Dorymenes as this governor; the identification is inferential. Kept separate from Ptolemy Macron (10:12), though some scholars equate them.

people.name: Dorymenes
people.description: Father of Ptolemy.

people.name: Aretas
people.description: Prince of the Arabians at whose court Jason was imprisoned.

people.name: Philip the Phrygian
people.description: Phrygian governor left in Jerusalem by Antiochus IV, who burned Sabbath-keepers in caves.

people.name: Andronicus
people.description: Governor left at Gerizim by Antiochus IV.
people.identity_note: Distinct from the Andronicus executed in 4:38.

people.name: Apollonius
people.description: 'Lord of pollutions' sent with 22,000 men who massacred Jerusalemites on the Sabbath.
people.identity_note: Greek 'Mysarch' (commander of Mysian troops) Apollonius; distinct from the governors of chs. 3-4 and from Apollonius son of Gennaeus (12:2).

people.name: An old man of Athens
people.description: Athenian sent by the king to compel the Jews to abandon their laws.
people.identity_note: Some read 'Geron the Athenian' as a proper name; WEB treats it as 'an old man'.

people.name: Eleazar
people.description: Aged principal scribe who chose death rather than eat swine's flesh.
people.identity_note: Merged with the Eleazar of 4 Maccabees 5-7 (same martyrdom; 4MA calls him a priest and lawyer); same new_id used in 4MA. Distinct from the priest Eleazar of 3MA 6 and from Eleazar of 2MA 8:23.

people.name: Mother of the seven brothers
people.description: Mother who encouraged her seven sons to die rather than break the law, and died last.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: First of the seven brothers
people.description: Spokesman of the brothers; tongue cut out and fried in a pan.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Second of the seven brothers
people.description: Scalped; affirmed the resurrection before dying.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Third of the seven brothers
people.description: Offered his tongue and hands, hoping to receive them back from heaven.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Fourth of the seven brothers
people.description: Tortured in the same way; denied a resurrection to life for the king.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Fifth of the seven brothers
people.description: Warned the king that God would torture him and his descendants.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Sixth of the seven brothers
people.description: Confessed that the Jews suffered for their own sins.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Seventh (youngest) of the seven brothers
people.description: Youngest son, who refused the king's offers and was treated worst of all.
people.identity_note: Same individual across 2MA (ch. 7) and 4MA (chs. 8-18); same new_id used in both files. The brothers are unnamed but each is individually distinguishable by his order of martyrdom.

people.name: Simon
people.description: Brother of Judas, a division commander.
people.identity_note: Brother of Judas (8:22, 14:17). 10:19-20 Simon is presumed the same. Reviewer: reconcile id with the 1MA census (Simon Thassi).

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Brother of Judas named as a division commander.
people.identity_note: 2MA names Simon, Joseph and Jonathan as Judas' brothers; 1 Macc 2:2-5 lists John (Gaddi) instead of Joseph. Possibly a scribal substitution for John, but kept as a separate entry. Distinct from the patriarch Joseph.

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Brother of Judas, a division commander.
people.identity_note: Reviewer: reconcile id with the 1MA census (Jonathan Apphus).

people.name: Eleazer
people.description: Read the sacred book aloud and led the first band against Nicanor.
people.identity_note: Probably Eleazar (Avaran) brother of Judas (1 Macc 2:5), but 2MA does not call him a brother and the Greek text is uncertain here (some witnesses read 'Esdris'). Kept separate; distinct from Eleazar the martyr.

people.name: Nicanor son of Patroclus
people.description: One of the king's chief friends, sent to destroy Judea and sell its people; defeated and fled to Antioch.
people.identity_note: Possibly the same as Nicanor the governor of Judea (14:12ff.); both are called 'thrice-accursed' (8:34, 15:3), and commentators often equate them, but 14:12 introduces him afresh as master of the elephants, so kept separate. Distinct from Nicanor governor of Cyprus (12:2).

people.name: Patroclus
people.description: Father of Nicanor.

people.name: Gorgias
people.description: Experienced captain, later governor of Idumaea, who fought Judas.

people.name: Timotheus
people.description: Enemy commander defeated by Judas, killed hiding in a cistern at Gazara.
people.identity_note: Killed in 10:37, yet a Timotheus is active again in ch. 12; treated as two entries (timotheus-2ma-b for ch. 12). 2MA is not strictly chronological, so they may be the same person narrated out of order.

people.name: Bacchides
people.description: Commander whose forces were defeated with those of Timotheus.
people.identity_note: Possibly the Bacchides of 1 Macc 7, but not clearly identified here.

people.name: The phylarch of Timotheus' forces
people.description: Unholy commander of Timotheus' forces killed by the Jews.

people.name: Callisthenes
people.description: Man who had set the sacred gates on fire, burned in a little house.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.description: Assyrian king whose army of 185,000 perished.

people.name: Philip
people.description: Foster brother of Antiochus IV who took his body home, fled to Egypt, and later became chancellor at Antioch.
people.identity_note: 9:29 and 13:23 merged as the same Philip (cf. 1 Macc 6:14-15, 55-56). Distinct from Philip the Phrygian.

people.name: Lysias
people.description: Guardian, kinsman and chancellor of Antiochus V; fought Judas and negotiated peace; killed by Demetrius.
people.identity_note: Called the king's 'brother' in a royal letter (11:22) as a court title.

people.name: Ptolemy Macron
people.description: Former Ptolemaic governor of Cyprus who dealt justly with the Jews and took poison when accused.
people.identity_note: Kept separate from Ptolemy son of Dorymenes.

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.description: Commander left with Simon and Joseph to besiege the Idumaean towers.

people.name: Chaereas
people.description: Commander of Gazara and brother of Timotheus, killed there.

people.name: Apollophanes
people.description: Killed with Timotheus and Chaereas at Gazara.

people.name: John
people.description: Jewish envoy to Lysias.
people.identity_note: Some identify him with John (Gaddi) brother of Judas; not stated.

people.name: Absalom
people.description: Jewish envoy to Lysias.
people.identity_note: Not David's son Absalom. Possibly the Absalom named as a father in 1 Macc 11:70, 13:11; not stated.

people.name: Quintus Memmius
people.description: Roman ambassador who wrote to the Jews.

people.name: Titus Manius
people.description: Roman ambassador who wrote to the Jews.

people.name: Timotheus
people.description: District governor who harassed the Jews, was routed by Judas and released on a promise to return hostages.
people.identity_note: See identity_note on timotheus-2ma-a.

people.name: Apollonius son of Gennaeus
people.description: District governor who would not let the Jews live in peace.

people.name: Gennaeus
people.description: Father of Apollonius.

people.name: Hieronymus
people.description: District governor hostile to the Jews.

people.name: Demophon
people.description: District governor hostile to the Jews.

people.name: Nicanor
people.description: Governor (commander) of the Cyprians hostile to the Jews.
people.identity_note: Distinct from the other Nicanors in 2MA.

people.name: Joshua
people.description: Leader in whose time Jericho fell.

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: Captain under Judas who destroyed Timotheus' garrison.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Dositheus of Bacenor's company (12:35) and Dositheus of 3MA.

people.name: Sosipater
people.description: Captain under Judas who destroyed Timotheus' garrison.

people.name: Dositheus
people.description: Horseman of Bacenor's company who nearly captured Gorgias.

people.name: Bacenor
people.description: Leader of a company in Judas' army.

people.name: Esdris
people.description: Leader of a Jewish force wearied in the battle against Gorgias.

people.name: Rhodocus
people.description: Jewish soldier who betrayed secrets to the enemy and was imprisoned.

people.name: Hegemonides
people.description: Left by Antiochus V as governor from Ptolemais to the Gerrenians.

people.name: Demetrius
people.description: Son of Seleucus who seized the throne, killed Antiochus V and Lysias, and sent Nicanor against Judas.

people.name: Alcimus
people.description: Former high priest who denounced Judas to Demetrius.

people.name: Nicanor
people.description: Former master of the elephants made governor of Judea by Demetrius; befriended then hunted Judas and was killed in battle.
people.identity_note: See identity_note on nicanor-son-of-patroclus. The festival of 13 Adar commemorates his defeat (15:36).

people.name: Posidonius
people.description: Envoy sent by Nicanor to make pledges of friendship.

people.name: Theodotus
people.description: Envoy sent by Nicanor to make pledges of friendship.
people.identity_note: Distinct from Theodotus of 3MA 1:2.

people.name: Mattathias
people.description: Envoy sent by Nicanor to make pledges of friendship.
people.identity_note: Not Mattathias the father of Judas.

people.name: Wife of Judas Maccabeus
people.description: Woman Judas married at Nicanor's urging.

people.name: Razis
people.description: Respected elder of Jerusalem who killed himself rather than be seized by Nicanor's soldiers.

people.name: Hezekiah
people.description: King of Judah in whose time an angel destroyed Sennacherib's army.

people.name: Mordecai
people.description: Named in 'the day of Mordecai' (Purim, 14 Adar).

excluded_names.Israel: nation (people of Israel), not the patriarch
excluded_names.Titus: part of Titus Manius (not the NT Titus)

notes: Chapters 1:1-2:18 are two prefatory letters; 1:13-16 gives a death of Antiochus that conflicts with ch. 9. Unnamed 'king of Persia' (1:20, 1:33-35) who commissioned Nehemiah is not recorded (not named). 'The king' in chs. 4-7, 9 is Antiochus IV and in 13 Antiochus V; refs for these include the clearest 'king' verses, not every pronoun. Group/minor unnamed figures skipped: priests of Nanaea (1:13-16), Heliodorus' angelic attackers (3:25-26, angels), the three senate envoys (4:44), two circumcising mothers (6:10), Antiochus' charioteer (9:4), the five heavenly horsemen (10:29), the horseman in white (11:8). Seven brothers are recorded individually (each is distinguishable by order of death in ch. 7) and share ids with 4MA. Shared ids with 4MA: eleazar-martyr, mother-of-seven-brothers, seven-brothers-son-1..7, antiochus-iv-epiphanes, onias-iii, jason-high-priest, seleucus-iv-philopator, simon-temple-guardian, apollonius-of-tarsus, ptolemy-vi-philometor. Reviewer: reconcile judas-maccabeus, simon-maccabeus, jonathan-maccabeus, lysias, gorgias, nicanor-*, timotheus-*, alcimus, demetrius-i-soter, antiochus-iv-epiphanes, antiochus-v-eupator, philip-foster-brother-of-antiochus-iv, ptolemy-son-of-dorymenes, bacchides-2ma8 with the 1MA census ids.

dated_events.event: Earlier letter of the Jews of Judea to the Jews of Egypt, written in the reign of Demetrius (II).
Date of the first prefatory letter urging the Egyptian Jews to keep the feast of tabernacles in Chislev (Hanukkah).
dated_events.note: The year 188 stands at the end of 1:9 in WEB; some editions attach it to the start of 1:10 (dating the second letter instead).

dated_events.event: Purification of the temple to be celebrated (stated in the second prefatory letter).
Sanctuary cleansed by Judas on the same day it had been profaned.
Letter of Lysias to the Jews after Judas' victory at Bethsuron.
Deadline for Jews to return home under amnesty in the king's letter.
dated_events.note: Year taken from the letter's own date in 11:33.

dated_events.event: Letter of King Antiochus (V) to the Jewish senate granting amnesty, carried by Menelaus.
dated_events.note: Historically this letter is often assigned to Antiochus IV (c. 164 BCE); the text places it under Eupator's reign.

dated_events.event: Letter of the Roman ambassadors Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius to the Jews.
News that Antiochus Eupator was invading Judea with Lysias.
Alcimus comes to King Demetrius (I) with a gold crown ('about' the 151st year).
dated_events.note: Text says 'in about the one hundred fifty-first year'.

dated_events.event: Day of Nicanor's defeat decreed as an annual festival, the day before the day of Mordecai.
